Middle Finger Buttress area (Amphitheatre Mtn routes)
Middle Finger Buttress area, above Upper Cathedral Lake
Middle Finger Buttress area (Amphitheatre Mtn routes)
Ka'aba Buttress / Pilgrimage to Mecca base area
Ka'aba Buttress / Amphitheatre Mountain routes area
Beverly Turnpike Trailhead (#1391)
waypoints.note: South/Teanaway-side approach via Beverly Creek and Fourth Creek trails toward Ingalls Creek, then bushwhack/scramble up to the SE side of the peak. Matches this route's own recorded GPS track almost exactly.

waypoints.name: PCT Trailhead at Stevens Pass (Hwy 2)
waypoints.note: Standard approach for Bulls Tooth: hike south on the PCT from Stevens Pass, then leave the trail near Lake Josephine to drop into Icicle Creek and climb ~1,800 ft into the Chain Lakes basin, then around Upper Chain Lake and up the talus couloir above it to a notch, finishing with a short Class 3 scramble to the higher, right-hand point.

waypoints.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.note: Standard approach: Snow Lakes Trail #1553 (~4.2 mi up Icicle Creek Rd from US-2 in Leavenworth) into the Enchantment Lakes basin, then via Perfection Lake to Prusik Pass, traverse NW to the Druid Plateau, then to the summit block (roughly 13-14 mi and over 7,300 ft of gain one-way).

waypoints.name: Pinto Rock Pullout (North Side)
waypoints.note: Roadside pullout on NF-77 (via NF-25 -> NF-28 -> NF-77 from Randle, WA) directly below Pinto Rock;
waypoints.directions: From Randle on US Highway 12, head south on SR 131 and follow NF-25 for 19.2 miles. Just past milepost 21, turn left at the Mosquito Meadows sign onto NF-28 and follow it 2.7 miles, then turn left onto NF-77. That last stretch is rough gravel, so drive it slowly; after about 2 miles Pinto Rock comes into view at a large pullout, and that pullout is the parking.

waypoints.name: Pinto Rock topout (approximate)
waypoints.note: Approximate - research confirms a short (~0.3mi) documented climbers trail from the pullout to the formation, but no exact topout coordinate was found; this reuses the pullout coordinate with a disclosed ~0.3mi uncertainty rather than a precise fix.

waypoints.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
waypoints.note: Drive ~1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then a short scramble up to Minidike's base.
waypoints.directions: From Dayton, follow North Touchet Road out of town toward Ski Bluewood; it is paved for roughly the first 15 to 16 miles, then turns to gravel as Forest Service Road 64 at the national forest boundary. The Dikes sit along that road in the East Fork Touchet River valley below Ski Bluewood, in the Walla Walla Ranger District of the Umatilla National Forest. The road continues to Ski Bluewood and stays in use through winter; snow on the crags and approach slopes is what limits climbing, to roughly May through October, sometimes from April. You do not park at this trailhead: for the Minidike, keep driving about 1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past it and park on the left, southeast side of the road just after you cross the bridge over the river.

waypoints.name: Minidike
waypoints.note: Smaller of the two closely-spaced fins at the core of The Dikes; park ~1.5 mi past the trailhead just after the river bridge, cross the road, scramble down the abutment, and follow the trail downstream on the NW bank.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Mine Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of Forest Road 4065; follow Sunrise Mine Trail to Headlee Pass then around Sperry Peak to the Vesper/Sperry basin.

waypoints.name: Vesper Peak north face
waypoints.note: Fish & Whistle starts from a large tree ~50 ft left of True Grit and climbs 5 pitches (5.10-) up the north face to near the summit.

waypoints.name: Cairned pass toward Copper Lake / start of ledge traverse
North Face ledge-access notch (near True Grit; Fish & Whistle starts ~50 ft further west)
Squire Creek Road Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access from Darrington via Squire Creek Road to blocked parking; road washed out ~2 mi in.
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to the Arlington exit and follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. Turn south on Madison Avenue to the T, go right on Darrington Street, and follow it as it becomes Squire Creek Road at the west end of town. Drive to the end of the road, about 1,100 feet, where a washout roughly two miles in gates it and blocks the parking area. Park at the gate; the old roadbed beyond it is walking only.

waypoints.name: Waterfall Basin (base of walls)
waypoints.note: ~3-3.5 hr to the basin and the base of Roan Wall via old roadbed, streambed, and a Squire Creek ford, below Three Fingers' east face. Salish Peak's base is farther on, up the left side of Roan Wall.

waypoints.name: Lunch Ledge belay (~300 ft on route)
Alpental Ski Area / Snow Lake Trailhead parking lot
waypoints.note: Alpental Ski Area parking lot, the shared start for all Guye Peak routes, including Improbable Traverse via the Ober Strasse approach.

waypoints.name: Guye Peak summit (south summit, has the summit register; traverse endpoint)

waypoints.name: Lake Serene Trailhead (Mount Index Rd / Trail 1068)
waypoints.note: Hike the Lake Serene trail then traverse talus/scree around the lake's south/west side into the Norwegian Buttress cirque; this is the only approach used for all routes in this cirque (Jötnar, Mjolnir, Bluebell, etc.).

waypoints.name: Jötunheim Wall Topout (Middle Peak)
waypoints.note: 16-pitch, Grade VI big wall (5.9 A3+) with bolted anchors and portaledge bivies; best climbed late July-early Sept before snowmelt turns pitches into waterfalls.

waypoints.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
waypoints.note: Drive ~1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then a short scramble up to Minidike's base.

waypoints.name: Cascade Pass Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Marblemount, follow the Cascade River Road 23.1 miles to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead, about 3,660 feet. Roughly the first third is paved and the rest is gravel, turning narrow and steep near the end.

waypoints.name: Mill Creek ford
waypoints.note: Ford Mill Creek just below the trail junction — last reliable, easy-to-reach water before the long climb toward Azurite.

waypoints.name: Mill Creek Trail junction
waypoints.note: Leave the Canyon Creek tread here and turn up the Mill Creek/Azurite Pass Trail; maintained trail effectively ends beyond this point.

waypoints.name: Overgrown Mill Creek Trail
waypoints.note: Tread disappears under heavy slide alder and downed timber left from the mine-era trail's disuse — expect a slow, scratchy alder-hacking bushwhack for several miles.

waypoints.name: Azurite Mine
waypoints.note: Flat ground amid the old defunct copper/silver mine workings on Mill Creek; the common overnight camp before pushing toward the Ballard basin.

waypoints.name: Azurite–Ballard basin
waypoints.note: Reached via roughly 3 more brush-choked miles above the mine; open basin at the base of Ballard's south slopes and a typical bivy before the summit push.

waypoints.name: South-face brush and gully route-finding
waypoints.note: Steep, loose terrain with several look-alike chutes low on the south face — picking the wrong gully here is the main way parties get cliffed out or turned back.

waypoints.name: Canyon Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Large parking lot on SR 20 just east of milepost 141, west of Rainy Pass. The trail follows Canyon Creek about 6 miles to the Mill Creek Trail junction, the start of this route's approach. The east-side line up the East Ridge starts elsewhere, at a locked gate on the Slate Creek road below Harts Pass (about 3,800 ft).

waypoints.name: Dosewallips Road washout parking
waypoints.note: Parking where the Dosewallips Road is closed at the washout. The Lake Constance climbers' trail leaves the closed road about 5 mi farther on, at roughly 1,450 ft.

waypoints.name: Dosewallips Road washout parking
waypoints.note: Same approach as the other standard-route variants; see Finger Traverse note.

waypoints.name: Dosewallips Road washout parking
waypoints.note: Same approach as Finger Traverse/North Chimney; Terrible Traverse is the original/harder crux crossing that Finger Traverse became the popular alternative to.

waypoints.name: Dosewallips Road washout parking
waypoints.note: "Same Dosewallips Road / Lake Constance approach as the other Constance routes, diverging higher up at Crystal Pass."

waypoints.name: Icicle Creek Road roadside parking (Hook Creek Drainage)
waypoints.note: Roadside parking used to access the Hook Creek Drainage spires above Icicle Creek.
waypoints.directions: From Leavenworth, take US-2 west to the edge of town and turn onto Icicle Creek Road. Follow it about 6.1 miles, roughly 2 miles past the Snow Lakes Trailhead, to the turnout on the left near a bridge. A path drops to the bridge and follows a private gravel road for a few hundred feet before a well-worn climbers' trail branches off; keep to it and keep quiet on the private stretch. That trail heads toward Yellowjacket Tower, then forks right into the Hook Creek drainage.

waypoints.name: The Mole (Edward Peak) North Face topout
waypoints.note: USGS name for this formation is Edward Peak; North Face follows an obvious crack system, 5.7, with a 3-rappel descent to the east.

waypoints.name: Hook Creek Drainage / Mole approach area
Luna Camp
waypoints.note: Alternative Big Beaver approach only, not the Hannegan line: established NPS backcountry campsite ~10 mi up the Big Beaver Trail (permit reserved at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center); base camp for leaving the maintained trail to find the Access/Luna Creek drainages.

waypoints.name: Luna Creek bushwhack
waypoints.note: Alternative Big Beaver approach only: off-trail ascent from Luna Camp through devil's club and alder thickets; one of the worst bushwhacks in the North Cascades, and it's easy to lose the drainage in the brush.

waypoints.name: Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine high camp
waypoints.note: High camp on the glacier's lateral moraine, reached from Whatcom Pass over the Whatcom Glacier, Perfect Pass and the Challenger Glacier; last reliable tent sites and meltwater before dropping toward Phantom Peak's southwest buttress.

waypoints.name: Southwest buttress saddle
waypoints.note: Gained via a roughly 1,000 ft descending traverse from the moraine camp; from here the route turns onto the pocket glacier on the buttress's southwest side.

waypoints.name: Bergschrund on the summit snow finger
waypoints.note: The pocket glacier's left-hand snow finger is cut by a bergschrund that's wide but shallow; parties crampon up slabby rock and crawl over the uphill wall to continue past it.

waypoints.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of Ruth Creek Rd / FR-32), via Hannegan Pass, Chilliwack River Trail, Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass to the SW side of Phantom Peak
waypoints.note: The main approach reaches this route from the west side of the range over Hannegan Pass; the alternative comes from Ross Lake up the Big Beaver Trail.

waypoints.name: Phantom Peak summit (Southwest/South Route, Class 4, easiest route, FA Fred & Helmy Beckey 1940)
Squire Creek Road Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access from Darrington via Squire Creek Road to blocked parking; road washed out ~2 mi in.
waypoints.directions: From I-5 take the Arlington exit and follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. In town turn south on Madison Ave, follow it to a T, turn right on Darrington Street, and stay on it as it becomes Squire Creek Road. Follow that road until a washout gates it off, roughly two miles in, and park there at about 1,100 ft. Everything past the gate is on foot up the old roadbed, with a flagged landslide crossing about five minutes from the car.

waypoints.name: Waterfall Basin (base of Roan Wall)
waypoints.note: Two approach pitches (bolted 5.8 slab, then low-5th groove) lead to the base of the actual Roan Wall from this point.

waypoints.name: Squire Creek Road Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access from Darrington via Squire Creek Road to blocked parking; road washed out ~2 mi in.
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to the Arlington exit, then SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. At the west end of town, go south on Madison Avenue to the T and turn right on Darrington Street, which becomes Squire Creek Road. Follow it to the washout gate at about 1,100 feet and park there — the road is washed out roughly two miles in and blocked to vehicles. From the gate the old roadbed continues on foot.

waypoints.name: Waterfall Basin (base of Roan Wall)
waypoints.note: Two approach pitches (bolted 5.8 slab, then low-5th groove) lead to the base of the actual Roan Wall from this point.

waypoints.name: Eagle Peak Saddle
waypoints.note: High point of the maintained trail; sweeping views of Mount Rainier, Adams, and St. Helens.

waypoints.name: Eagle Peak Trailhead (Longmire, Nisqually Suspension Bridge)
waypoints.note: Reached from Longmire: park at the Lodge/Museum lot, walk past staff housing and across the Nisqually Suspension Bridge; trailhead is just over the bridge.

waypoints.name: Pinto Rock Pullout (North Side)
waypoints.note: Same pullout as the other North Side routes; the approach trail is extremely steep and loose.
waypoints.directions: From Randle on US Highway 12, head south on SR 131 and follow NF-25 for 19.2 miles. Just past milepost 21, turn left at the Mosquito Meadows sign onto NF-28 and follow it 2.7 miles, then turn left onto NF-77. That last stretch is rough gravel, so drive it slowly; after about 2 miles Pinto Rock comes into view at a large pullout, and that pullout is the parking.

waypoints.name: Pinto Rock topout (approximate)
waypoints.note: Approximate - research confirms a short (~0.3mi) documented climbers trail from the pullout to the formation, but no exact topout coordinate was found; this reuses the pullout coordinate with a disclosed ~0.3mi uncertainty rather than a precise fix.

waypoints.name: Surprise Lake
waypoints.note: Trail switchbacks above the lake to join the PCT. Surprise Lake sits at 4,500 ft. An earlier pin for it sat 5.2 mi west, the same ~4.5 mi westward error this route's other waypoints were already corrected for.

waypoints.name: Trap Pass
waypoints.note: PCT junction; the climbers path to Thunder Mountain and Slippery Slab Tower leaves directly from the top of the pass.

waypoints.name: Base of Slippery Slab Tower
waypoints.note: Corrected — an earlier coordinate (47.665,-121.22) sat ~4.5mi west of Trap Pass instead of continuing toward the tower, likely a data entry error. This pin (47.668645,-121.126119, elev 6356ft) matches the area's own registered location.

waypoints.name: Slippery Slab Tower NE Face Topout
waypoints.note: Corrected — an earlier coordinate (47.6636,-121.2226) was ~4.5mi off; this pin is cross-checked against the area's own registered location. Two-pitch 5.4; Pitch 2 diagonals left into a gully to a large boulder near the top.

waypoints.name: Tunnel Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: FS Rd 6095, ~13.2 mi east of Skykomish off US-2; approach is Tunnel Creek Trail -> PCT (Hope Lake) -> south to Trap Pass -> climbers trail to NE base of tower

waypoints.name: Snow Lakes
waypoints.note: Trail continues up past the lakes toward Enchantment Basin.

waypoints.name: Viviane Campsite (Lake Viviane)
waypoints.note: Reached after climbing ~6,400 vertical ft; limited campsites on either side of the lake outlet, adjacent to the crag.

waypoints.name: Base of Prusik Peak south face (approximate)
waypoints.note: Approximate — no reliable topout coordinate was found, so this reuses the Viviane Campsite coordinate; the climbing zone is right at the base of Prusik Peak's south face/west ridge near the camp.

waypoints.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead (Trail #1553)
waypoints.note: From Snow Lakes TH, hike Snow Lakes Trail #1553 up through Nada Lake/Snow Lakes and the Enchantment basin to Lake Viviane, where the crag sits directly alongside the trail.

waypoints.name: Barclay Creek crossing / leave trail
waypoints.note: About a quarter mile past the trailhead, cross Barclay Creek on a stout logjam ~200 yards upstream of an old spur road, then bushwhack toward an overgrown corrugated culvert marking the start of the Tailgunner climbers' path.

waypoints.name: Rocky knob on climbers' path
waypoints.note: Old logging-road tread gives way to a rockier, more open knob roughly 2.8 hours up from the trailhead; route-finding gets easier here as the path steepens into Tailgunner Ravine. The knob sits at ~3,600 ft; position is estimated, not surveyed.

waypoints.name: Waterfall ravine
waypoints.note: The 'infamous waterfall ravine' cliff band at ~4,000 ft: a Class 2-3 scramble around a waterfall in the ravine that forces a short descent and re-ascent; slick rock when wet. Position is estimated, not surveyed.

waypoints.name: Brushy cliff-band weakness
waypoints.note: Leave the Tailgunner Couloir here through a brushy weakness in the cliff band to gain the crest of the west ridge; grassy slopes and firm snow patches persist into early summer. Position is estimated, not surveyed.

waypoints.name: Tailgunner Pass
waypoints.note: Broad saddle between Gunn Point and Tailgunner reached after ~3,000 ft of gain; couloir approach and the upper Gunn Basin camps converge here. Position is estimated, not surveyed.

waypoints.name: West ridge gendarmes / cornice headwall
waypoints.note: Follow the ridge crest over minor gendarmes; a relic cornice headwall near the summit dome requires careful, exposed scrambling, especially with lingering snow. Position is estimated, not surveyed.

waypoints.name: Barclay Lake Trailhead (FR-6024)
waypoints.note: End of FR-6024 (Barclay Creek Road); shared trailhead for Barclay Lake, Gunn Peak, Gunn Point, Tailgunner, and Wing Peak approaches via Barclay Creek and Tailgunner Pass.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.directions: Park at the informal pullout on the north shoulder of SR-20, about 1.2 miles east of Washington Pass and a short walk east of the small roadside pond — the same start used for the East Face. No permit is needed here.

waypoints.name: Lexington Tower East Shoulder (topout)
waypoints.note: This route climbs the slabs right of the East Face route on Lexington Tower, Washington Pass.

waypoints.name: Pinto Rock Pullout (North Side)
waypoints.note: Same pullout/approach as Sidewinder and Clast from the Past; Top Gun is a toprope reached by lowering from Sidewinder's anchor chains to the roof lip, i.e. same base approach, not a separate trailhead.
waypoints.directions: From Randle on US Highway 12, head south on SR 131 and follow NF-25 for 19.2 miles. Just past milepost 21, turn left at the Mosquito Meadows sign onto NF-28 and follow it 2.7 miles, then turn left onto NF-77. That last stretch is rough gravel, so drive it slowly; after about 2 miles Pinto Rock comes into view at a large pullout, and that pullout is the parking.

waypoints.name: Pinto Rock topout (approximate)
waypoints.note: Approximate - research confirms a short (~0.3mi) documented climbers trail from the pullout to the formation, but no exact topout coordinate was found; this reuses the pullout coordinate with a disclosed ~0.3mi uncertainty rather than a precise fix.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Mine Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of Forest Road 4065; follow Sunrise Mine Trail to Headlee Pass then around Sperry Peak to the Vesper/Sperry basin.

waypoints.name: Vesper Peak north face
waypoints.note: True Grit is a 5-pitch, 5.8 line up the north face, one of the original moderate routes on the wall.

waypoints.name: Cairned pass toward Copper Lake / start of ledge traverse
North Face ledge-access notch (True Grit start)
Squire Creek Road Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access from Darrington via Squire Creek Road to blocked parking; road washed out ~2 mi in.
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to the Arlington exit and follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. In town, go south on Madison Avenue to the T, turn right on Darrington Street, and continue as it becomes Squire Creek Road at the west end of town. Follow the road to the parking area at about 1,100 feet where a washout roughly two miles in gates it off; there is no driving past that point. Everything beyond is on foot, starting with the old roadbed and a flagged landslide crossing about five minutes along.

waypoints.name: Waterfall Basin (base of Waterfall Buttress)
waypoints.note: Buttress sits left of the major slab waterfall; hike talus to the buttress toe. Base often buried under avalanche debris early season.

waypoints.name: Meadow rising traverse
waypoints.note: Boot path climbs through an open meadow then angles into a rising traverse aiming for the crest of Whistler's south ridge; faint tread, easy to lose in fog.

waypoints.name: South ridge gain point
waypoints.note: Boot path tops out on the level section of Whistler's south ridge here; from this point the route follows the ridge and connecting gullies toward the summit.

waypoints.name: 6,800 ft ridge/gully split
waypoints.note: Ridge steepens; here parties can cut left across gullies onto the gentler southwest slope as an easier alternative to staying directly on the ridge crest.

waypoints.name: Summit ridge scramble band
waypoints.note: Class 2-3 terrain mixes downsloping slabs and loose gravel on ledges just below the summit ridge; a helmet is worth carrying for rockfall and slip potential here.

waypoints.name: Rainy Pass Trailhead (PCT North parking lot, SR-20)
Dose Forks
waypoints.note: West Fork Dosewallips Trail splits off the main Dosewallips Trail here at the river confluence; reliable water and a designated camp with toilet and bear wires.

waypoints.name: Diamond Meadows Camp
waypoints.note: Last established backcountry camp before Honeymoon Meadows; river-adjacent water source, elevation estimated by interpolating between Dose Forks and Honeymoon Meadows.

waypoints.name: Honeymoon Meadows Camp
waypoints.note: Forested backcountry campsite just below the actual meadows, the standard base camp for the White Mountain scramble day, at about mile 15.

waypoints.name: Anderson Pass
waypoints.note: Divide between the Quinault and Dosewallips drainages and trail junction toward Anderson Glacier; leave the maintained trail here and head south toward White Mountain — little to no water at the pass itself.

waypoints.name: Heather/scree slopes below the summit ridge
waypoints.note: Steep heather and talus that often retains hard, unmarked snow patches into midsummer; carry an ice axe and expect route-finding on this class 2 terrain.

waypoints.name: Dosewallips Road end (closed-road parking)
waypoints.note: From this road-end, the route continues via bike/foot up West Fork Dosewallips River to Honeymoon Meadows before the Class 2 scramble to White Mountain's summit.
